reading.body:
This campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity across 175,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, this would support roughly 825 racks; at 100 kW per rack for GPU-dense inference workloads, roughly 330 racks. The published capacity places it sixth among Texas facilities that disclose power figures, and sixth represents 6.9% of the state's 475 MW of published data center IT load.

The certifications qualify this campus for security-sensitive workloads including FISMA federal systems, HIPAA health data, and PCI DSS payment systems. TIA-942 indicates it meets a standard building classification for data centers. The combination suggests the campus is architected to host regulated enterprise and government workloads rather than indicating AI infrastructure specifically.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities but only 19 publish power capacity. This campus is one of the disclosed nineteen. The gap between mapped count and published count means most facilities in the state report no IT load figure, so the state's actual capacity is unknown. Among operators willing to state figures, CyrusOne San Antonio ranks in the top tier.
